transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been troubling you or what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… thanks. I guess I’m here because lately I just feel like I’m always running hot, if that makes sense. Like I can’t really shut the motor off.

I’ve tried to chalk it up to the job, you know, being a firefighter and all, but it’s been starting to cause some problems at the firehouse. Nothing I’m proud of. I just figured I should talk to somebody before it gets worse… if that makes sense.
Have you been having intrusive thoughts, memories, or flashbacks about a specific event that’s been bothering you lately?

Um… not really, no. I mean, I’ve seen some rough stuff on calls, obviously, but I wouldn’t say there’s one specific thing that keeps replaying or anything like that.

At least, not that I’ve noticed. It’s more… I don’t know, just hard to turn my brain off sometimes. But flashbacks, like feeling like I’m back there? No, I don’t think so.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried about a number of different things, more days than not, even when there isn’t an immediate reason to be concerned?

I don’t know… I wouldn’t say I’m, like, constantly worried about everything, no. I mean, I’ve got normal stuff on my mind, work and bills and family things, but I don’t think it’s this big anxiety thing.

Unless I’m misunderstanding what you mean. It’s more… my head feels busy, but not always worried, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed that you’re not getting as much pleasure or interest out of things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, work, or time with friends and family?

I don’t think so… not in a big way, anyway. I still like being around people I care about, and I don’t feel like everything’s gone flat or anything.

I mean, I probably don’t get to stuff as much as I should, but I think that’s more life and work than me not enjoying it. Does that make sense?
Have you been having trouble falling asleep or staying asleep, even when you’re tired?

I mean… sometimes, yeah, but I don’t know if I’d call it a major problem. With the job, sleep can be kind of all over the place anyway, so it’s hard to tell what’s “normal,” you know?

I can usually get some sleep eventually. I might lie there for a while with my mind still going, but… I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Would you say that you often feel tense or keyed up, like you can’t relax, even when there isn’t anything specific to worry about?

Yeah… I guess I do get that way, though I don’t know if I’d call it worry exactly.

Like in command meetings, if I have to sit there for a while, it feels like my body’s revving too high. I’m sitting in the chair, but I’m kind of fighting the urge to get up and walk the bay, check the rigs, do something useful instead of just staying planted there.

I can usually keep it together, I think, but inside I’m pretty keyed up. Is that what you mean?
Has anyone close to you, like coworkers or family members, ever mentioned that you seem restless, fidgety, or unable to sit still, especially when you're not doing any specific task?

Yeah… I mean, people have mentioned it. Not like in a harsh way, usually, but someone’ll say, “You’re bouncing your leg again,” or they’ll notice I’m clicking a pen.

In meetings especially, if I’m just sitting there, I’ll be shifting around in the chair or messing with whatever’s on the table, and half the time I don’t even realize I’m doing it until someone points it out.

I try not to be distracting, obviously. But yeah, I guess it’s noticeable sometimes.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy most of the time, even when you haven’t been doing anything physically demanding?

Not most of the time, I don’t think. I mean, with the job, I can be tired after a shift or if the schedule’s been rough, but that feels… kind of expected.

On days where I haven’t really done much physically, I don’t usually feel wiped out for no reason. At least, not that I’ve noticed. Is that the sort of “low energy” you’re asking about?
Have you found yourself getting more irritable or easily annoyed lately, even over small things?

I don’t think more than usual, no. I mean, everybody gets annoyed sometimes, and with work there are moments where little things can get under your skin, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been snapping at people or anything like that.

At least… not that anyone’s really called me out on. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about your performance at work or feeling like you’re not meeting expectations, even when others might not see a problem?

Yeah… I do worry about it. I try not to make it sound bigger than it is, because I’m not trying to make excuses, but it’s started to affect how people see me at the firehouse.

I got pulled into a performance and safety meeting, which was… embarrassing, honestly. The issue was basically that the crew can’t always count on me to keep track of the details the way I should. And even if nobody’s yelling at me day to day, I can feel that trust slipping a bit.

I’ve been hoping to move toward a leadership role, and now it feels like that might be getting away from me because of this. I don’t know if that answers it right, but yeah, I think about it a lot.
Do you find that you worry a lot about your performance or feel anxious about not meeting expectations, even when things seem to be going fine?

Yeah… I mean, I try not to overthink it, and sometimes things probably are going fine on the surface. But it’s hard not to worry now because it’s already started costing me some trust at the firehouse.

I got pulled into a performance and safety meeting, which was pretty embarrassing. It wasn’t like I’m not trying—it’s more that the crew can’t always count on me to keep track of the details consistently. And I’ve been hoping to move into more of a leadership role, so now it feels like that chance is kind of slipping away.

So… yes, I do worry about whether I’m meeting expectations. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it’s definitely on my mind.
Do you find yourself worrying about a number of different things — not just work — even when there isn’t an immediate reason to be concerned?

I’m not sure I’d say a number of different things, no. It’s mostly the work stuff that gets in my head.

I mean, I’ll worry about normal life things here and there, like anybody does, but I don’t think I’m sitting around anxious about everything for no reason. At least I haven’t really noticed it that way. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed that even on days when you haven’t done anything physically taxing, you still feel unusually tired or like you don’t have much energy?

I don’t think so… not in a way I’d call unusual. I mean, with my job, being tired kind of comes with the territory sometimes, so it’s hard to separate.

But on days where I haven’t really done much physically, I can’t say I’ve noticed being wiped out for no reason. At least not enough that it stands out to me. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you find it hard to control your worry, even when you try to tell yourself it’s not that big of a deal or there’s nothing you can do about it right now?

I don’t know that I’d say it’s hard to control exactly. I mean, when it comes up, I can usually tell myself, “Okay, there’s nothing you can do about this right now,” and move on enough to function.

It might still sit in the back of my mind a little, but I’m not sure it’s like… uncontrollable worry. I don’t want to overstate it. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Would you say that your worry about your performance at work has been happening more days than not for at least several months now?

I’m not totally sure I’d put it that strongly. I do think about work performance, yeah, especially after certain shifts or if I feel like I could’ve handled something better.

But “more days than not for several months”… I’d have to really think about that. It’s not like I’m tracking it, you know? It may come up a fair amount, but I don’t want to say yes if that’s making it sound bigger than it is.
Would you say that you feel restless or physically unable to relax on most days, even when there’s no immediate stressor or problem to deal with?

Yeah… I mean, I guess I do notice that. I wouldn’t say I’m, like, bouncing off the walls all day or anything, but sitting still can be pretty uncomfortable.

Like during command meetings, if we’re just sitting there for a while, it feels like my body is kind of revving too high. I’ll be thinking, “I need to stand up, walk the bay, check the rigs,” just… do something besides stay planted in the chair.

I can usually keep it together, I think, but relaxing physically doesn’t always come easy. Is that the kind of restlessness you mean?
Have you been diagnosed with or experienced symptoms of any other mental health conditions, such as panic attacks, extreme fear of social situations, or trauma-related stress?

Not that I know of, no. I mean, I haven’t been diagnosed with anything like that.

I don’t think I have panic attacks or, like, an extreme fear of social situations. And trauma stuff… I don’t know, I’ve seen rough things with the job, obviously, but I wouldn’t want to claim I have that unless that’s really what it is.

So I guess my answer is no, or at least nothing that’s been formally diagnosed. Is that fair?
Would you say that your restlessness — like feeling keyed up or having a hard time relaxing — happens on most days, even when things are calm or there’s no big stressor going on?

Yeah… I think so, more than I’d probably like to admit. Even when nothing major is going on, sitting still can feel pretty hard.

Like in command meetings, I’m not trying to be difficult or anything, but after a while it feels like my body is just revving too high. I’m sitting there thinking I should stand up, walk the bay, check the rigs—just do something instead of staying planted in that chair.

I can usually keep it contained, I think, but yeah, that feeling shows up even when things are technically calm. Does that answer what you mean?
How long have you been feeling restless or keyed up like this — would you say it’s been happening nearly every day for at least six months?

Yeah… I think it’s definitely been at least six months. Honestly, if I’m being accurate, it’s probably been more like a year and a half — maybe around a year and five months.

It seemed to really become a problem after the longer rotating shifts started, and then with the extra documentation and the drone duties getting added on. I don’t want to overstate it, but that’s when I started noticing it most days. Does that timeline make sense?
